title: Independent audit of the SAT grid inverse and exact-root-count claims
objective: Independently reconstruct and audit the claims in the SAT grid inverse / Laurent-support research cluster. Determine exactly what is proved, what is only a candidate construction, and whether the stated verification-hardness and exact-count statements have correct reductions and bit-complexity accounting. Do not infer P=NP or P!=NP.
scope: Reconstruct the definition of the normalized SAT grid, its inverse/candidate inverse, and the exact verification predicate.
Check the claimed exponential expanded Laurent monomial support against the succinct representation size.
Check whether the proposed single-query exact grid-root count recovers #SAT, including multiplicities and normalization factors.
Check the promise-gap coNP-hardness reduction, parameter sizes, promise preservation, and both directions of the reduction.
deliverables: Precise formal statement of each claim with all input encodings and promises.
Line-by-line reduction audit, including bit lengths and construction time.
Classification of each result as proved, plausible but incomplete, false, or not assessable from the supplied artifacts.
Small counterexample or independently reproducible check for any failed identity.
Exact location of the first unresolved step and a corrected theorem statement if possible.
acceptance_criteria: Distinguish circuit-size, expanded monomial-count, dense-degree, and input-bit-length costs.
Do not treat coNP-hard verification as a P-vs-NP resolution.
Account for coefficient bit lengths, arithmetic precision, multiplicities, and promise gaps.
Every reduction must be polynomial in the stated source input length.
Include exact citations and theorem numbers for imported results.
